start.speaker: Rook
start.text: Far as you go, gumshoe. The elevator's private, and Mr. Kanzaki isn't taking walk-ins — 'specially not the one who's been asking the docks about drums.

n1.speaker: Rook
n1.text: So turn around. Or give me a reason not to put you down the stairs the quick way.

choices.text: Kanzaki's finished. Don't go down with him.
We've met. The Neon Dragon, back when this started.

brawl.speaker: Rook
brawl.text: Ha. The tired man wants to dance. Your left arm's been ticking since you walked in, detective — I can hear the servo skipping. Come on, then. Show me what the city left you.

brawl_win.speaker: Rook
brawl_win.text: ...Alright. Alright. You hit like the rent's overdue. My arm doesn't glitch, and it still wasn't enough — that's a compliment, from me.

brawl_win2.speaker: Rook
brawl_win2.text: Go up. Bleed on his carpet, not mine. And when you're up there — remember the Zheng cartel would trade their teeth for whatever's got you this stupid. Elevator's yours.

brawl_lose.speaker: Rook
brawl_lose.text: There it is. The arm quits right when you need it — that's the city's whole design, detective, wrote small in your own wiring. Sit down before you fall down. Try the door again when you've got a better idea than your fists.

r9.speaker: Rook
r9.text: ...Let me see that. That's a city seal. Reclamation Board.

r9b.speaker: Rook
r9b.text: Huh. All this time I figured I was guarding a rich man. Turns out I'm guarding a *subcontractor.* That's not a syndicate problem, detective. That's a him problem, and I don't take a bullet for a him problem.

discover.title: Rook's Tip
discover.desc: Kanzaki's own enforcer read the city seal on Order R-9 and stepped aside. His parting advice: the Zheng cartel has wanted Kanzaki's harbor contract for years. A page like R-9, in the right rival hands, is worth more than any headline — and it wouldn't stop the drums. It'd just change whose name is on them.

r9c.speaker: Rook
r9c.text: One more thing, free of charge. The Zheng cartel would trade their teeth for that page — they've wanted Kanzaki's harbor for years. You could walk out of here rich instead of righteous. Elevator's yours. Try not to bleed on the marble.

pragmatic.speaker: Rook
pragmatic.text: Finished. Sure. Men like him are always finished, right up until they're not and you're floating face-down in the harbor you were so worried about. Come back when 'finished' is a piece of paper and not a feeling.

callback.speaker: Rook
callback.text: I remember. You were greener then. You've got the look now — the one that doesn't expect to like what's upstairs. Doesn't change my job, though.

bye.speaker: Rook
bye.text: Smart. Rain's better company than what's up top anyway.
